units: pixels (x right, y down, original resolution) and seconds; no metric scale assumed

camera.motion: static (no pan/shake; background identical frame to frame, consecutive-frame difference ~0 once the typewriter is at rest, frames 25-29)
camera.perspective: Still-life desk scene viewed roughly front-on at about desk height. The falling typewriter moves vertically in the image plane; its pixel width stays 289-292 px through the whole fall (frames 0-10), i.e. constant depth -> a single px scale is valid for the fall. Its apparent height grows 113 -> 167 px during the fall because the camera sees its underside at the top of the frame and its top/keyboard when it is lower (viewing-angle change, not a depth change). Desk top recedes in perspective (front edge near bottom of frame, back edge y~945).

typewriter.description: Black vintage portable typewriter (silver/white keys, carriage with two paper-guide plates on top). The only moving object.
typewriter.reference_point: bbox_cx, bbox_cy (centre of the mask bounding box) = best 2D estimate of the rigid-body origin/centre; centroid_x/y (mask pixel mean) also given

rest_extents_px_frames_24_29.note: rotated (yawed) after the tumble, so wider than in the fall; the mask's right edge includes ~10-15 px of contact shadow, zoomed visual reading gives width ~328 px, height ~172 px

events.name: release / start of fall
events.note: already moving downward 0->1 (centre +8 px), so release is at or just before frame 0

events.name: last frame fully in the air
events.note: bottom edge y=974, desk contact level ~1026-1031

events.name: impact with desk
events.note: first frame touching desk (bottom edge 1031); impact occurs between frames 10 and 11 (t 0.417-0.458)

events.name: tips up onto its front edge (rocks toward camera)
events.note: top edge rises 862 -> 796; bbox centre moves up 946.5 -> 909.5 and right 1009 -> 1021

events.name: highest point of tip-up / direction change
falls back flat with a yaw turn

static_objects._note: pixel boxes [x0, y0, x1, y1] at frame 0, read from a 100-px grid overlay; accuracy ~+-10 px
